transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I just can’t seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. Like at work. I'm a loan officer, and lately, I'll just sit at my desk staring at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list, and I end up rereading the same line over and over. It's so frustrating. 

Actually, the other day I was looking at this file for a young couple buying their first home—a nice little ranch house over on Elm Street. Do you know that area? They have those beautiful old oak trees lining the sidewalks. My sister used to live near there, and the leaves in the fall were just a nightmare to rake. She ended up buying this fancy gas leaf blower, but it was so loud the neighborhood association complained and she had to return it. Such a hassle getting the refund, too. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the office. Yeah, I just keep putting off making my client calls because lately, even simple decisions just feel so much harder than they should.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

I suppose so, yes. Most days there’s just this... this dull heaviness sitting with me. It doesn't really seem to matter what I'm doing. Like, even when I’m at the community center or out in my garden. Those are places that always used to lift me up. 

Actually, my garden is usually my pride and joy—I planted these beautiful hydrangeas last spring. The blue ones, you know? You have to get the soil acidity just exactly right or they turn pink. I was buying the aluminum sulfate at the hardware store, and the cashier—this young kid, couldn't have been more than eighteen—tried to tell me I was buying the wrong thing for roses. I had to explain to him I wasn't growing roses! Kids these days just don't get trained properly at those big box stores. It's a real shame, they just throw them on the register with no background knowledge. 

But... oh, I'm sorry, where was I? Right, feeling down. Yeah, even when I'm doing those things I usually love, I just feel like I’m going through the motions. I just have this smile pasted on my face, but underneath, it's just heavy.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried lately?

I wouldn't say anxious, really. Not like that heart-racing kind of panic or anything. Just... maybe a little unsettled sometimes? But not worried in a big way. 

Though, speaking of being unsettled, my neighbor's dog has been barking at all hours of the night lately. It's a little terrier mix, cute as a button, but it just yaps and yaps. I think they leave it out on the patio when they work the night shift. I tried talking to them about it, but they're renting, and you know how renters can be—here today, gone tomorrow. The landlord is this older gentleman who used to own the bakery downtown. Oh, his eclairs were just out of this world! The custard was so rich. He sold the place a few years back to a corporate chain, and it's just not the same. The pastry cream tastes artificial now, like it comes out of a plastic bucket. 

But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, right, worrying. No, I don't think I'm particularly anxious. Just tired and heavy, mostly.
Do you find that you're no longer enjoying activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Well, I guess I'm still doing the things I usually do. Like my gardening, like I mentioned, and my book club. We meet every other Thursday at the library. The new librarian is lovely, she always makes sure we have the quiet room in the back. Though last week, the heating was acting up again. It's an old building, you know, built back in the thirties, and the radiators clank so loudly you can barely hear yourself think. We were trying to discuss this historical fiction novel set in World War II—oh, the author did such a wonderful job with the research, especially about the rationing. My mother used to tell me stories about rationing when I was little. She kept all her old ration books in this beautiful cedar chest at the foot of her bed. It smelled so wonderful every time you opened it... 

But, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, about enjoying things. Um, I don't know if I've stopped enjoying them, really. I still go to book club and I still plant my flowers. I just... I don't know, it's just that heavy feeling is always there while I'm doing them.
Do you feel like you're getting as much pleasure out of gardening and book club as you used to?

I suppose I'm not really sure. It's hard to measure exactly how much pleasure you get out of something compared to before, isn't it? It’s a bit like when people come into my office—I'm a loan officer, mostly dealing with home equity and credit counseling these days—and they try to justify taking out a massive second mortgage for a swimming pool or a new kitchen. They talk about how much joy it'll bring the family, but I always tell them they have to look at the amortization schedule. The interest rates right now are just doing a number on everybody. 

I had this one young couple in last Tuesday, sweet as pie, thinking they could afford a total remodel on a starter home. They actually brought me a little tin of snickerdoodle cookies to try and butter me up. The wife said her grandmother made them. And I have to say, I haven't had a proper snickerdoodle in years! The secret, you know, is you have to use a pinch of cream of tartar. If you just use baking powder, they get all cakey and lose that nice chewiness in the center. My aunt Martha used to make them for every family reunion, right alongside her ambrosia salad, which had those little mini marshmallows in it... 

Wait, I'm sorry, my mind is just wandering everywhere today. What were you asking me? Oh, about enjoying my gardening and the club. I don't know, I guess I just haven't really noticed if the pleasure is less or not. I'm still doing them all, it's just... I'm there, but I'm not really fully feeling it, if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, like you're just going through the motions?

Well, it's been quite a while now. I'd say... gosh, since my close friend Sarah passed away. That was a little over two years ago. We used to do everything together, you know. She was the one who actually got me into the book club in the first place. She had this wonderful habit of picking out the most obscure biographies. I remember she made us read this huge, thick book about the man who invented the modern zipper. Who would have thought there was a whole book about zippers? But it was fascinating! It had all these diagrams of the early prototypes, and apparently, they were originally used for boots before they ever put them on clothing. 

Sarah used to wear these beautiful leather boots in the winter. She bought them on a trip to Italy... Florence, I think? Or maybe it was Milan. She always said the leather goods in Italy were unmatched, and you really had to haggle at the street markets to get the best price. She was a master haggler. Me, I could never do it. I just pay whatever the price tag says. It always feels so rude to argue with someone over a few dollars, especially when they're just trying to make a living. Like the boy who mows my lawn, Tommy. He raised his rate by five dollars this summer because gas prices went up, and I just said, "Of course, Tommy, that makes perfect sense." He's saving up for a car, you see. A used Honda Civic. Good, reliable cars, Hondas. My brother had one that ran for almost three hundred thousand miles before the transmission finally gave out...

Oh, dear, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry. You asked how long I've felt this way. Yes, it's been since Sarah died, so a little over two years of just... feeling like this.
Have you lost any weight unintentionally over the past few months?

No, I don't think so. My clothes all still fit exactly the same as they always have. I buy most of my trousers from this little catalog that comes in the mail, they have these wonderful elastic waistbands that don't pinch when you're sitting at a desk all day. Because sitting at a desk, looking at spreadsheets and credit reports, well, it really does a number on your lower back. I tried one of those ergonomic chairs once, the ones where you sort of kneel on it? But it just made my knees ache. My doctor—my regular doctor, Dr. Evans—told me I should take up water aerobics for my joints. The community center has a class on Tuesday mornings, but the instructor, Brenda, she plays the music so terribly loud. It's all that disco music from the seventies. I mean, I liked the Bee Gees as much as anyone back then, but at eight in the morning, it's just a bit much, don't you think? And the chlorine smell just lingers in your hair all day, no matter how much you wash it. I buy this special clarifying shampoo from the salon down the street, the one with the pink awning... 

Oh, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Weight? Right. No, my weight hasn't changed at all.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasurable?

Well, I wouldn't say there's anything I've completely stopped enjoying or given up on. I'm still keeping up with everything. Like the gardening, I was actually just out there yesterday looking at my hydrangeas. You know, they're supposed to be blue, but they've been turning this sort of washed-out pink color lately. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, told me I need to make the soil more acidic, so she brought me over this huge bag of used coffee grounds. She works over at that diner on Main Street, the one with the neon sign that's always buzzing. To be honest, their coffee is just dreadful, it always tastes burnt if you ask me. 

I'm much more of a tea drinker myself. Earl Grey, usually. I have this lovely little ceramic teapot I bought at a craft fair years ago. The woman who made it painted these tiny little cornflowers all over it by hand. It must have taken her hours and hours to do. I always wonder how people have the patience for that kind of detailed work. I certainly don't, especially not with my eyes these days. I had to get bifocals last year, and let me tell you, trying to read a client's credit report through the bottom half of your glasses is an absolute nightmare. The numbers just sort of swim together if you don't hold your head at the exact right angle...

Oh, goodness, I've completely lost the thread again, haven't I? I am so sorry, my brain is just a sieve today. You were asking if there's anything I don't find pleasurable anymore. No, I don't think there's anything specific. I'm still doing all my usual activities and hobbies, I just... I don't think I've dropped anything at all.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite over the past few months?

No, my appetite is exactly the same as it's always been. I still eat my regular meals. I usually have a bowl of oatmeal in the morning, the kind with the little dried apples in it? Though honestly, I think they've been putting fewer apples in the packets lately. Shrinkflation, they call it. I saw a whole segment about it on the morning news while I was getting dressed for work. They were showing how orange juice cartons are smaller now but cost the exact same amount. It's just terrible for people on a fixed income, trying to make a budget work. I see it all the time at the office. People come in, and they're just drowning in credit card debt because groceries cost an arm and a leg now. 

I had this one client, Mr. Henderson, just the sweetest older gentleman, and he had maxed out three different cards just buying basics. He used to be a carpenter before he retired, built these beautiful custom cabinets. He showed me pictures of a kitchen he did back in the nineties, all solid cherry wood with these intricate brass handles. You just don't see craftsmanship like that anymore, do you? Everything now is just that cheap particle board you have to assemble yourself with a little Allen wrench. I bought a bookshelf like that once, and it took me three hours to put it together, and it still leans a little to the left...

Oh, I'm doing it again. I am so sorry, I don't know why I keep rambling on like this. You were asking about my appetite. Yes, it's completely normal, no changes at all.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

I feel like we just touched on this a moment ago, didn't we? With the gardening and all that? No, I really haven't lost interest in anything. I'm still doing all my usual things. 

Like my cross-stitch, I'm actually working on a piece right now for one of the junior loan officers at my branch. She's having her first baby, and I'm making this little bib with yellow ducks on it. Yellow is such a cheerful color, but let me tell you, it is terribly hard to match if you run out of thread halfway through. I had to go to three different craft stores last weekend just to find the exact right shade of lemon yellow. The cashier at the third store—the one over by the old shopping mall that's mostly empty now—she had her hair dyed the most shocking shade of blue. It looked exactly like a Blue Jay. We get a lot of Blue Jays at the feeder outside my kitchen window. They are so aggressive, though, they just swoop in and chase all the little finches right away. I tried buying that special safflower seed because they say the bigger birds don't like it, but it's so terribly expensive now. Everything is, really. I see it on the credit reports I review every day, people are just charging their basic necessities because a bag of birdseed or a gallon of milk costs so much...

Oh, my goodness, listen to me. I'm doing it again! I am so sorry, my mind is just bouncing all over the place today. What were you asking? Oh, right, losing interest. No, no, I still enjoy my cross-stitch and the bird watching and everything else just fine.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

No, my weight has been exactly the same. My clothes all fit just like they usually do. I still weigh myself every so often on this old dial scale I've had for years in the bathroom. It has this little faded floral pattern on the mat. My sister, Brenda, she just bought one of those fancy digital ones that connects to her phone. I told her, why on earth does your bathroom scale need Wi-Fi? But she loves all those gadgets. She has a watch that tracks her steps and her heart rate and tells her when to stand up. 

If I had something buzzing at my wrist to stand up while I was at work, I think I'd throw it right out the window. I'm glued to my desk at the office, especially lately. We just got this new software for processing the debt consolidation loans, and it is just an absolute disaster. The screen freezes right when you're in the middle of entering a client's liabilities, and then you have to call the IT department. They always put you on hold with that terrible elevator music, the kind that sounds like it's being played on a synthesizer from the eighties. I must have sat there for twenty minutes yesterday just listening to it loop over and over... 

Oh, dear, I've completely derailed myself again, haven't I? I am so sorry. You were asking about my weight. No, no weight loss at all, it's stayed perfectly steady.
Do you have difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep at night?

No, my sleep is completely fine. I don't have any trouble falling asleep, and I usually sleep right through the night. I have this wonderful down comforter that keeps me perfectly warm, even when the house gets drafty. It's an older house, you know, built in the fifties, and the windows really need to be replaced. I had a guy come out to give me an estimate last month, and you wouldn't believe the price he quoted me. It was absolutely astronomical. 

He tried to tell me it was because of supply chain issues with the glass, but I know a sales pitch when I hear one. I see it all the time with my clients. They get talked into these expensive home improvement projects and put the whole thing on a high-interest store card. Next thing they know, they're sitting in my office crying because the promotional interest rate expired and their minimum payment tripled. It just breaks my heart. There was this one young couple just last week, they bought a fixer-upper and decided to redo the whole master bathroom...

Oh, for heaven's sake. Look at me, I'm off on another tangent. I apologize, I really don't mean to keep wasting your time with all these stories. You asked about my sleep. Yes, I sleep perfectly well, no issues there at all.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened in your life?

No, I wouldn't say I feel guilty about things. I mean, we all have little regrets here and there, but nothing that keeps me up at night or makes me feel bad about myself. I try to just keep moving forward, you know? 

Like with my sister, Brenda. We had this silly argument last Thanksgiving about how to make the stuffing. She insists on using that boxed mix, the one with the little seasoning packet, but I always make it from scratch with the recipe our mother used. It takes stale bread and fresh sage—you have to use fresh sage, the dried kind just tastes like dust. I grow it in a little pot on my windowsill, right next to the African Violet that I've managed to keep alive for three years now. They are so fussy about watering, African Violets. You can't get the leaves wet or they get these ugly brown spots. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he waters his plants with a little turkey baster to make sure the water goes right into the soil. He's such a character. He's always out in his driveway polishing that antique Buick of his. It's a beautiful car, cherry red, but he never actually drives it anywhere. Just polishes it and puts the cover back on. I always wonder what the point of having a car like that is if you never take it out on the road. It's like those people who buy expensive china and just leave it in the cabinet...

Oh, dear me. I've done it again, haven't I? I am so sorry, my mouth just runs away without my brain sometimes. You were asking about feeling guilty. No, I really don't struggle with guilt. I just try to do my best every day.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to live or of harming yourself?

No, no, I've never had any thoughts like that. I just keep plodding along, you know? Even when I'm feeling down, I just make myself get up and go to work. The routine helps, I think. 

Although, the routine has been completely upended lately because of the construction on 4th Street. They've had the right lane closed for three weeks now, and the traffic backs up all the way past the old cinema. You remember the old cinema? The one with the real marquee where they had to put the letters up with a long pole? They tore it down to build a pharmacy, which is just ridiculous because there's already a pharmacy right across the street. A big chain one, open twenty-four hours. I went in there the other night because I needed some cough drops—the cherry ones, not the menthol, the menthol always makes my eyes water—and the girl at the register looked like she was about twelve years old. She couldn't figure out how to scan my coupon on my phone. I tried to show her, but the screen kept going dark...

Oh, goodness gracious. I am so sorry. I'm rambling again, aren't I? I don't know why I keep doing that. You were asking about... oh, right, thoughts of harming myself. No, absolutely not. I would never do anything like that.
Do you feel like your heavy feelings and lack of motivation are interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Well, yes, I suppose they are. I’ve actually started postponing my client follow-ups at the credit office. I just look at the list of names and I can't seem to bring myself to pick up the receiver. Our office phones are so frustrating anyway, the buttons always stick. Especially the number four. I told the building manager about it, but he just sprayed some WD-40 on it and called it a day. It smells awful now. He’s a nice enough man, but he wears these terribly loud Hawaiian shirts, even in the dead of winter. He says it reminds him of his honeymoon in Maui thirty years ago. I've never been to Hawaii myself. I always thought the flight would be too long. I can't sit still for that many hours, my knees start to ache. 

I used to walk a lot to keep my joints limber, but... well, I've actually stepped back from the walking-club outings I used to make a point of attending. And the local gallery events, too. I just don't have the drive to go anymore. I used to love the watercolor exhibits they put on downtown. They always served those little cheddar cheese cubes with the frilly toothpicks. You don't see those frilly toothpicks much anymore, do you? It's all bamboo skewers now, very modern and minimalist. My niece had her whole wedding in that minimalist style. Barely any flowers, just lots of geometric metal shapes and white linens... 

Oh, dear me. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Talking about toothpicks and weddings. I am so sorry. But yes, to answer your question, it is interfering. I'm just not keeping up with my work calls, and I've stopped going to my usual outings.
Would you say your heavy feelings and lack of motivation are affecting your daily life most of the time?

Well, yes, like I was just mentioning, it really is most of the time now. Almost every single day I just sit there postponing those client follow-ups at the credit office. And it's been weeks since I've been to any of the gallery events or my walking-club outings. 

It's a shame, too, because I had just bought these very expensive orthopedic sneakers specifically for that walking club. They have those extra-thick foam soles, you know, the ones that sort of rock forward when you take a step? They make you look like you're wearing little boats on your feet, to be completely honest, but the podiatrist swore by them. Dr. Shoemaker, his name was. Isn't that a funny name for a foot doctor? Shoemaker. He has his office over on Elm Street, right next to where the old German bakery used to be. The one that sold those wonderful, dense pumpernickel loaves. You really can't find good pumpernickel anymore, it's all just dyed brown bread at the supermarket these days. I tried to make my own once, but the dough is so sticky and heavy, it nearly burnt out the motor on my KitchenAid mixer...

Oh, goodness me. There I go again, off into the weeds about bread and mixers. I am so sorry, I don't know where my focus goes. But yes, to answer you, it's pretty much all the time now that I'm putting off my work and skipping the things I used to make a point of attending.
How long have you been experiencing this lack of motivation and heavy feeling?

Well, it’s been quite a while now. I’d say it started right around the time my close friend passed away, which was a little over two years ago. 

She was such a dear person. We actually met at the credit office, back before everything was computerized. We used to have these huge green filing cabinets, the heavy metal ones that would pinch your fingers if you didn't close them just right. I actually still have a little scar on my left index finger from one of those drawers. It was the 'M through P' drawer, I'll never forget it. We had so many clients with last names starting with M back then. Miller, Moore, Mitchell... I don't know why, maybe it was just the demographics of the neighborhood at the time. That neighborhood has changed so much, too. They put in one of those fancy coffee shops right on the corner where the old dry cleaner used to be. A cup of plain black coffee costs five dollars now! And they don't even give you a proper ceramic mug if you sit down, just a paper cup with a cardboard sleeve that always slips off. I spilled hot coffee all down the front of my good wool coat last winter because of one of those flimsy sleeves, and it cost an absolute fortune to get the stain out... 

Oh, goodness gracious. I am so sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Rambling on about filing cabinets and coffee cups. I just can't seem to keep my thoughts in a straight line today. But yes, to answer your question, it's been a little over two years, ever since I lost my friend. That's when this heavy feeling really set in.
Has your heavy feeling and lack of motivation been continuous since your friend passed away, or have you had periods where you felt better in between?

Well, I... I suppose I haven't really noticed any breaks in it. It just feels like one long, gray stretch since she passed. We used to do everything together, you know. We even took a trip to the Poconos once, back in the late nineties. The hotel we stayed at had these heart-shaped bathtubs. Can you imagine? Heart-shaped! It was so tacky, but we laughed until we cried trying to figure out how to sit in the thing without sliding down into the point. The water pressure was terrible, though. Just a trickle. It took nearly an hour to fill it up, and by the time it was full, the water was lukewarm. I've always hated lukewarm baths. My mother used to say that a hot bath could cure anything from a cold to a broken heart. She swore by Epsom salts, the kind that smelled like eucalyptus. I bought a bag of it recently, thinking it might help my aching knees, but the scent was so strong it gave me a terrible migraine. I had to keep all the blinds drawn for two days. The sunlight just felt like ice picks behind my eyes...

Oh, dear. I'm so sorry. I've completely lost the thread again, haven't I? Heart-shaped tubs and Epsom salts. I apologize. But, um, to answer your question... no, I haven't really had any periods where I felt better. It's just been a constant, heavy weight ever since she died.
Has your heavy feeling lasted for more than two years continuously since your friend passed away?

Well, yes, like I said, it's been a little over two years now since she passed. It's just been this... constant thing since then. Two years is a long time, isn't it? It feels even longer when the days just drag on. I remember when we first met, I thought two years at that credit office would be an eternity, but I ended up staying there for decades. Decades! And the things I've seen in that office. You wouldn't believe the excuses people give when they can't make a payment. One gentleman, Mr. Henderson, he told me his dog actually ate his payment book. Not his homework, his payment book! And he brought in the mangled remains of it in a little plastic sandwich bag just to prove it. It was a Pomeranian, too, one of those little fluffy things that look like they couldn't hurt a fly, let alone chew through heavy cardstock. I always preferred larger dogs myself. Golden Retrievers, mostly. They have such gentle mouths, they can carry a raw egg without breaking it. I saw that on a television program once. It was on PBS, I think. They always have such wonderful nature documentaries on Sunday evenings. I used to watch them with a cup of chamomile tea, but lately, even making tea feels like too much effort. The kettle is just so heavy...

Oh, my goodness. I'm doing it again. I am so, so sorry. I just... my mind just wanders off. But yes, to answer you, it's been going on continuously for over two years now, ever since I lost her.
Do you feel like your heavy feelings and lack of motivation are significantly impacting your ability to carry out daily activities?

Well, yes, I suppose they are. I’ve actually started postponing my client follow-ups at the credit office, which is very unlike me. I used to pride myself on being so prompt. Promptness is a virtue, my father always said. He was a watchmaker, actually. Can you imagine? Working with all those tiny little gears and springs all day. He had this magnifying glass that he wore over one eye, it made him look like a very serious cyclops. He used to fix all the clocks in our house, and we had a lot of them. There was this one grandfather clock in the hallway that chimed every quarter hour. It drove my mother absolutely up the wall. She finally made him stop winding the chime mechanism after I was born because it kept waking me up. I was a terrible sleeper as a baby. Still am, really. I toss and turn all night, tangling up the sheets until they're just a knot at the bottom of the bed. I bought those Egyptian cotton sheets recently, the ones with the high thread count that are supposed to be so luxurious, but honestly, they just feel stiff to me. Maybe they need to be washed a few more times. I use that lavender-scented detergent, though I'm starting to think the smell is a bit too cloying...

Oh, dear me. I've gone right off the rails again, haven't I? Grandfather clocks and bedsheets. I am so sorry, Doctor. But yes, it is impacting me. Besides the work follow-ups, I’ve also completely stepped back from the gallery events and the walking-club outings I used to always make a point of attending. It's just... too much effort now.

doctor.intent: determine presence of depressed mood
doctor.question: Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days there’s this dull heaviness sitting with me, and even when I’m at the community center or in my garden, places that used to lift me up, I feel like I’m just going through the motions with a smile pasted on.

patient.answer:
I suppose so, yes. Most days there’s just this... this dull heaviness sitting with me. It doesn't really seem to matter what I'm doing. Like, even when I’m at the community center or out in my garden. Those are places that always used to lift me up. 

Actually, my garden is usually my pride and joy—I planted these beautiful hydrangeas last spring. The blue ones, you know? You have to get the soil acidity just exactly right or they turn pink. I was buying the aluminum sulfate at the hardware store, and the cashier—this young kid, couldn't have been more than eighteen—tried to tell me I was buying the wrong thing for roses. I bought those Egyptian cotton sheets recently, the ones with the high thread count that are supposed to be so luxurious, but honestly, they just feel stiff to me. Maybe they need to be washed a few more times. I use that lavender-scented detergent, though I'm starting to think the smell is a bit too cloying...

Oh, dear me. I've gone right off the rails again, haven't I? Grandfather clocks and bedsheets. I am so sorry, Doctor. But yes, it is impacting me. Besides the work follow-ups, I’ve also completely stepped back from the gallery events and the walking-club outings I used to always make a point of attending. It's just... too much effort now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent heavy feelings, lack of motivation, and decreased interest in activities they once enjoyed, lasting for over two years, align more closely with a diagnosis of Mild Depressive Episode (F32.0). The patient does not exhibit significant weight loss, insomnia, or psychomotor agitation, which might suggest a more severe depressive episode.
